title_en: Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Establishing Maritime Courts in Coastal Port Cities

articles.content_en: I. A maritime court shall be established in certain coastal port cities as needed. The establishment, alteration or abolition of a maritime court shall be decided by the Supreme People's Court. The setup of the adjudication organs and administrative offices of a maritime court shall be prescribed by the Supreme People's Court.

II. A maritime court shall be responsible to the Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the city where it is located. The adjudication work of a maritime court shall be subject to the supervision of the Higher People's Court of the place where it is located.

III. A maritime court shall have jurisdiction over maritime cases and maritime trade cases of first instance, and shall not accept criminal cases or other civil cases. The division of the jurisdictional areas of each maritime court shall be prescribed by the Supreme People's Court. Cases on appeal against judgments and rulings of a maritime court shall be under the jurisdiction of the Higher People's Court of the place where the maritime court is located.

IV. The president of a maritime court shall be appointed or removed by the Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the city where it is located upon the proposal of the chairman of such Standing Committee. The vice presidents, division chiefs, deputy division chiefs, judges, and members of the adjudication committee of a maritime court shall be appointed or removed by the Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the city where it is located upon the proposal of the president of the maritime court.
